newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-London, Frankfurt stocks down; dlr advances.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-London, Frankfurt stocks down; dlr advances.

text.p: London and Frankfurt chalked up steep losses in low volumes on Friday with most of Europe closed for a public holiday and with no pointers coming from Wall Street's dull overnight finish.

In currencies, the dollar climbed more than half a yen as concern grew that the turmoil in many SouthEast Asian currencies would hit the Japanese economy. Sterling was stronger against the mark and dollar.

London and Frankfurt, two of the only bourses operating on the Assumption Day holiday, had a rough morning after poor performances on Thursday despite relief that U.S. July consumer prices showed little threat to the bull markets on both sides of the Atlantic.
London's blue-chip FTSE 100 index was down 0.8 percent by midday but the broader-based FTSE 250, characterised by medium-sized, manufacturing companies, was 22.7 up at 4,712.
"The manufacturers are continuing to catch up and outperform the big blue-chip stocks," said one dealer.
Volume was a meagre 190.8 million shares. "It's very quiet and the futures have really let us down on the FTSE 100," said another dealer.
Among shares weighing on the market was satellite TV broadcaster BSkyB, which was down 25 pence to 445 by midday after profits failed to meet expectations.

In Frankfurt, stocks fell nearly two percent in quiet floor trade that tracked losses in post-bourse dealings on Thursday. The 30-share DAX index was down 86.36 points at one stage, at 4,145.07 points.

In currencies, trade was quiet in a market that was overshadowed by the weaker yen. The Japanese currency fell against the mark and sterling, and was down to 118.45 yen to the dollar, compared with 117.85 in late dealings on Thursday.

The benchmark Japanese bond yield fell to a record low of 2.065 percent overnight. Analysts said the yen, once the safe-haven currency of Asia, has finally fallen victim to the currency crisis sweeping the region.

Traders said that given the magnitude of the economic and financial ties between Japan and other Asian nations and the poor investment climate in Japan, continued turmoil in Asia is likely to trigger yen sales against the U.S. dollar.

On Thursday Indonesia's central bank said it was lifting the intervention band with immediate effect, virtually making the rupiah a freely floating currency -- the latest among Asian nations since Thailand's similar announcement on July 2.
"The yen's weakness is due to more than just one factor but it is hard to see anything positive for the yen out of the Asian currency crisis," said Kit Juckes, currency strategist at NatWest Markets.
"About half of Japan's trade is within Asia, so it's losing some of its competitive edge there, even though Hong Kong and China are more important for Japan," Juckes said.
The dollar was virtually unchanged against the mark although speculation about a German rate rise is likely to intensify in the run-up to next week's Bundesbank council meeting, analysts said.
"This should tend to keep the mark relatively well supported through the early part of the week," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist at Bank of America in London.

Sterling was also up against the mark and dollar in early Europe compared with late Thursday's European levels, though traders said the pound was still vulnerable to market worries over a possible rise in German interest rates.
The pound was at 2.9405 marks against Thursday's late European level of 2.9300 and versus the dollar was at $1.5967 from $1.5872.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.8407 marks and 118.45 yen, compared with 1.8417 and 117.85 in late European trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 48.0 points at 4,943.3.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was down 78.57 points at 4,152.86.
PARIS - Closed.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $323.50 an ounce , compared to Thursday's close of $326.25. Silver was down eight cents at $4.42.
